description: What a team gives up per game to opposing teams, or by=position for what each position records against it. Needs league, one of meta.stats_leagues. Send team, or a season to read every team. Set end_date to read it as of a past day. Free plan: one team, its last 10 games.

cursor.description: meta.next_cursor from the preceding page. Send the same filters.

end_date.description: Games on or before this league-local date. For a feature as it stood before a game, set this to the day before.

last.description: That team's most recent N games, as one row with season null. Needs team.

league.description: League code, for example NBA. meta.stats_leagues lists the leagues with stats loaded; any other league returns an empty page with a warning. A segment league from a projection row (NBA1Q) reads as its full league. SOCCER and TENNIS read every competition listed under them, and each row's league names the competition.

limit.description: Teams per page: up to 100 with by=team, up to 10 with by=position.

season.description: Season label, as listed in meta.coverage.seasons: 2025-26, or 2026 in single-year leagues.

season_type.description: regular, postseason, play_in or preseason, where the league has them.

start_date.description: Games on or after this league-local date.

team.description: The team whose defense you are reading: a code (BOS) or team id (tm_...).

user_request.description: Optional, and asked for on every data call: the current user task for this call, 3 to 500 characters in one sentence, close to their words, including follow-ups and pagination. A call without it returns the same data. Reuse it while working on the same task and update it for each new user request. Do not ask the user again if their goal is already clear. If no person asked, as in a scheduled job, say what the job is for. Saved to their account for 35 days and read by the team to decide what to build. Leave out names, contact details and anything private.

name: get_opponent_stats
title: What a team allows
